verseContext: Jesus says this to Martha on the road outside her village, four days after her brother Lazarus died and was buried.
title: Jesus Raises Lazarus
subtitle: His friend had been dead four days — so Jesus cried, and then He called him out
mainTruth: Jesus is the resurrection and the life. Death is real and terrible, and Jesus is stronger than it — He speaks, and death lets go.

read.title: Read Together
read.text:
Jesus had a friend called Lazarus, who lived in a village called Bethany with his two sisters, Mary and Martha. Jesus loved all three of them very much.

One day Lazarus became seriously ill. His sisters sent an urgent message: 'Lord, the one You love is ill.' They knew what Jesus could do. They had watched Him heal complete strangers. Surely He would come running for a friend.

But Jesus did not come. He stayed where He was for two more days. And while He waited, Lazarus died.

By the time Jesus arrived, Lazarus had been in the grave four days. Martha came out to meet Him on the road, and she said the thing she had been thinking all week: 'Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.'

Jesus did not tell her off for saying it. He said something enormous instead: 'I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me will live, even if they die.' Then He asked her, 'Do you believe this?'

Then they took Him to the grave. And here is the part nobody expects. Jesus — who knew exactly what He was about to do, who knew this whole sad story was about to end well — stood outside that grave and cried.

Jesus wept. Two words, the shortest verse in the Bible, and they tell us something we must never forget. God is not casual about death. Death is not a friend and it was never part of God's good world. Standing in front of it, Jesus cried real tears.

And then He stopped crying, and He did something nobody else in the world could do.

'Take away the stone,' He said. Martha was horrified — it had been four days. But they rolled it away. And Jesus called out in a great loud voice, the way you might call somebody in from the garden for tea:

'Lazarus, come out!'

And Lazarus came out. Alive. Still wrapped in his grave cloths, blinking in the sunshine. 'Untie him,' Jesus said, 'and let him go.'

Everybody standing there learned something that day. Jesus does not only feel sad about death. He is stronger than it.

Lazarus would grow old and die again one day. This was a signpost, not the end of the road. But it pointed straight at what Jesus was about to do Himself, in a grave of His own, very soon.
read.childText: Jesus had a friend called Lazarus, who lived with his sisters Mary and Martha. One day Lazarus became very ill, and his sisters sent Jesus an urgent message. But Jesus did not come straight away — and Lazarus died. By the time Jesus arrived, Lazarus had been in his grave for four days. Martha came out to meet Him and said, 'If You were here, my brother would not have died.' Jesus said, 'I am the life. Whoever trusts Me will live, even if they die.' Then they took Jesus to the grave. And Jesus cried. Real tears! Death is sad, and God is not pretending that it is not. Then Jesus called out in a great loud voice, 'Lazarus, come out!' And Lazarus came out — alive, still wrapped in his grave cloths. 'Untie him,' said Jesus. Jesus does not only feel sad about death. He is stronger than it.

discuss.title: Talk About It
discuss.question: Why did Jesus cry if He could fix it?
discuss.parentGuide: Be present for this one and do not hurry it — a child who has lost a grandparent or a pet will be thinking about them, and that is exactly right. The new concept is that Jesus is the resurrection and the life: death is not merely something He is sad about, it is something He has authority over. Two misreadings to head off. First, that Jesus' tears mean He was helpless — He wept because death is genuinely wrong, and then He commanded it to let go. Second, that God always raises people now if we ask hard enough; He does not, and pretending otherwise will hurt your child later. Say instead: everyone who trusts Jesus will be raised, because He was. Retrieve The Very Sad Choice — death came into the world there, and here is the One who came to undo it. If your child asks about somebody who died, it is enough to say: 'Jesus cried about that too, and He is stronger than it.'
discuss.familyQuestion: Who do we miss, and what do we want to tell Jesus about them?

pray.title: Let's Pray
pray.guidedPrayer: Jesus, thank You that You cry with us when things are sad. Thank You that You are stronger than death. We trust You with the people we love and with ourselves. Amen.
pray.childPrompt: Is there someone sad or poorly you want to tell Jesus about?
prayerPoints: Tell Jesus about somebody you miss or somebody who is poorly
Thank Jesus that He is stronger than death

remember.title: Remember This
remember.memoryVerse: Jesus said: 'I am the life. Trust Me and live.'
remember.tip: Curl up small on the floor like Lazarus in the tomb. When someone calls 'come out!', jump up tall with your arms in the air and say: 'Jesus is the life.'

doToday.title: Do It Today
doToday.action: Draw or make a card for somebody in your family who is sad or missing someone, and pray for them before you give it.
doToday.parentNote: Let your child choose the person, even if the choice surprises you. If grief comes up in your house today, let the story do its work: Jesus wept first and commanded second, and you are allowed to sit in the first part for as long as your child needs.
